If a smooth function on a nonempty open convex domain has positive-definite Hessian, satisfies the affine maximal equation, and its graph is complete in the induced Euclidean metric, then the domain is all of $\mathbb R^n$ and the function is a positive-definite quadratic polynomial plus an affine term. exact_statement:
theorem affine_bernstein
    (n : ℕ) (hn₃ : 3 ≤ n) (hn₉ : n ≤ 9)
    (Ω : Set (Space n)) (hΩne : Ω.Nonempty) (hΩopen : IsOpen Ω)
    (hΩconvex : Convex ℝ Ω) (u : Space n → ℝ)
    (hu : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ u Ω)
    (hpos : ∀ x ∈ Ω, (hessian u x).PosDef)
    (hmax : AffineMaximalOn Ω u)
    (hcomplete : EuclideanGraphComplete Ω u) :
    Ω = univ ∧
      (∃ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (b : Space n) (c : ℝ),
        A.IsSymm ∧ A.PosDef ∧
        ∀ x, u x = (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (∑ i : Fin n, ∑ j : Fin n, x i * A i j * x j)
          + (∑ i : Fin n, b i * x i) + c) ∧
      (∃ e : (Space n × ℝ) ≃ᵃ[ℝ] (Space n × ℝ),
        e '' standardParaboloid n = graph Ω u)
